After studying at Queen's Academy and passing her exams, she gave up a college scholarship to stay at Green Gables and teach locally when Marilla's eyesight began to fail, reconciling with her rival Gilbert Blythe when he gave up the Avonlea school so she could have it.

As an Avonlea teacher, Anne accidentally sold her neighbor's cow, accidentally applied rug dye to her nose before hosting important guests, and rejected an unromantic marriage proposal sent on behalf of Billy Andrews.
Over the course of her college years, Anne refused a romantic marriage proposal from Gilbert Blythe, spent time teaching at Valley Road, and successfully published a short sketch.
At the end of her college life, Anne rejected a proposal from her wealthy suitor, Roy Gardner, after realizing in the moment that she did not love him.

She excelled academically, forming an intense rivalry with Gilbert Blythe, starting a story club, and eventually tying for first place on the Island's Queen's Academy entrance examinations.
After earning the Avery scholarship at Queen's and enduring the devastating death of her beloved Matthew from a sudden heart attack, Anne chose to stay at Green Gables to support Marilla.

Anne later pursued higher education at Redmond College, securing her financial future thanks to a thousand-dollar bequest from the late Miss Josephine Barry and finally reading a collection of her deceased parents' love letters in her birthplace of Bolingbroke.

Throughout her young adulthood, Anne navigated several clumsy marriage proposals—including ones from Jane Andrews on behalf of her brother Billy, Sam, and her long-time suitor Royal Gardner—while mistakenly believing Gilbert Blythe was engaged to someone else.
Upon learning that Gilbert was near death from typhoid fever, Anne finally recognized her deep romantic feelings for him.
Following his miraculous recovery, Anne accepted Gilbert's proposal in Hester Gray's garden, happily agreeing to marry him.
